problems.title: Which warp, which lane
problems.solution: $t = 5 + 3 \times 16 = 53$, warp $\lfloor 53/32 \rfloor = 1$, lane $53 - 32 = 21$. Warp 1 holds rows 2 and 3 of the block.

problems.title: A block of 100

parts.prompt: Active lanes in the last warp?
Fraction of the block's issue capacity wasted, in %?

problems.solution: (a) 4, (b) $100 - 96 = 4$, (c) $28/128 = 21.9\%$ of lane-slots are empty in every instruction the block issues.

problems.title: An awkward shape
problems.solution: 60 threads make 2 warps; warp 1 holds $t = 32..59$, 28 lanes. $t = 32$ is $x = 12$, $y = 1$: warp 1 starts mid-row, so its lanes straddle rows 1 and 2 unevenly.

problems.title: Three dimensions
hints: $t = x + y B_x + z B_x B_y$.
problems.solution: $t = 3 + 16 + 32 = 51$: warp 1, lane 19. Each warp here is exactly one z-slice ($8 \times 4 = 32$).

problems.title: Enough warps?
problems.statement: Each warp does $C = 25$ cycles of independent work per memory access; memory latency is $L = 600$ cycles. An SM has 4 schedulers.

parts.prompt: Warps per scheduler needed to keep it busy?
Only 48 warps are resident on the SM. Scheduler utilisation, in %?

problems.solution: (a) $(25 + 600)/25 = 25$. (b) 12 per scheduler: each issues in at most $12/25 = 48\%$ of cycles. The fix is more independent work per warp (bigger C, or ILP), or more warps if limits allow.

problems.title: Resident warps and the block limit
problems.statement: An SM holds at most 2,048 threads and 16 blocks.

parts.prompt: Resident warps with blocks of 64 threads?

hints: Which limit binds first: threads or blocks?
problems.solution: (a) 16 blocks × 64 = 1,024 threads = 32 warps: the block limit binds. (b) 16 × 96 = 1,536 threads = 48 warps. (c) 16 × 128 = 2,048 threads = 64 warps: both limits meet. Small blocks can leave half the SM empty.

problems.title: ILP instead of warps
problems.statement: As in the chapter: $L = 400$, $C = 20$. Now each warp has two independent loads in flight per iteration (instruction-level parallelism 2), so each warp keeps two requests outstanding during a latency period.
hints: Each warp now covers twice the work per latency period: divide by 2.
problems.solution: $420/(2 \times 20) = 10.5$, so 11 warps per scheduler, inside the limit of 16. Two independent loads per warp did what 10 extra warps would have done. Volkov's paper (Part 2) turns this into a design principle.

problems.title: The slowest lane decides
problems.statement: Each lane's load independently hits in cache (30 cycles) with probability 0.99, or misses (400 cycles).

parts.prompt: Fraction of warp loads that take 400 cycles, in %?
Average load latency seen by a thread in isolation, in cycles?

hints: A warp waits for its slowest lane: P(at least one miss) = 1 − 0.99³².
problems.solution: (a) $1 - 0.99^{32} = 27.5\%$ of warp loads wait the full 400 cycles. (b) One thread alone would average $30 + 0.01 \times 370 = 33.7$ cycles. A 1% miss rate per lane becomes a 27% stall rate per warp.

problems.title: Warp latency in expectation

parts.prompt: Expected latency of a warp load, in cycles?
Per-lane miss rate that would make half of all warp loads miss, in %?

problems.solution: (a) $30 + 370 \times 0.2750 = 131.8$ cycles, nearly 4× the per-thread average. (b) $(1-p)^{32} = 0.5 \Rightarrow p = 1 - 0.5^{1/32} = 2.14\%$. Lockstep amplifies rare events: this is why GPU code is designed so that a warp's lanes behave alike.

problems.title: Lockstep, officially
problems.statement: Since Volta, NVIDIA warps have independent thread scheduling.

parts.prompt: Code that exchanges data between lanes through shared memory, assuming they run in lockstep, must now…
options: Do nothing: lanes of a warp are still in lockstep
Use __syncwarp() (or *_sync intrinsics) to synchronise the lanes explicitly

parts.prompt: To be portable across vendors, warp-size-dependent code should use…

problems.solution: (a) __syncwarp() and the *_sync intrinsics name the lanes that must participate; __syncthreads() works but synchronises the whole block, which is more than needed. (b) warpSize: AMD wavefronts are 64 wide on CDNA.
